questions.stem: Which amino acid is unique in undergoing rapid oxidative deamination by glutamate dehydrogenase, releasing free ammonia?
questions.explanation: Most amino groups are funneled to glutamate by transamination, and glutamate is the only amino acid rapidly deaminated oxidatively. A: Alanine gives its amino group to α-KG via ALT. B: Aspartate donates nitrogen at argininosuccinate synthetase in the urea cycle. D: Glutamine is cleaved by glutaminase in the liver. E: Lysine isn't transaminated; it loses its amino group by a different deamination.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman who always disliked meat and milk becomes confused and drowsy after starting a high-protein diet. Ammonia is 240 µmol/L, plasma glutamine is high, citrulline and blood urea are low, urine orotic acid is high, and ALT/AST are normal. Her mother's brother died at 4 days of age. What is the diagnosis?

options.B: OTC deficiency in a female carrier

questions.explanation: Low citrulline with high orotic acid means carbamoyl phosphate is made but not passed to ornithine and spills into pyrimidine synthesis; X-linked inheritance explains the affected uncle and the mosaic female carrier. A, C: With CPS I or NAGS missing, no carbamoyl phosphate is made, so orotic acid is low. D: The block is after citrulline, so citrulline would be high. E: Arginase acts last, so citrulline and arginine would not be low.

questions.stem: Why does a protein-rich meal speed up the urea cycle?

options.E: Glutamate and arginine raise N-acetylglutamate, which activates CPS I

questions.explanation: NAGS makes N-acetylglutamate from acetyl-CoA and glutamate, and arginine activates NAGS; the meal supplies both, and N-acetylglutamate is the essential activator of CPS I, the rate-limiting enzyme. A: Arginine activates NAGS, not CPS I directly. B: N-acetylglutamate acts on CPS I. C: The control point is CPS I, the first step, not arginase. D: Arginine, not aspartate, activates NAGS.

questions.stem: Which pair of amino acids is exclusively ketogenic?
questions.explanation: Leucine and lysine are the only exclusively ketogenic amino acids: their carbon skeletons can't make glucose. A, C: These amino acids are glucogenic or both, not exclusively ketogenic. D, E: These yield pyruvate or TCA intermediates, so they are glucogenic.

questions.stem: A newborn screened on day 1 has a normal phenylalanine level. By 6 months, the infant has a musty urine odor, fair hair and light skin, seizures and developmental delay. Which enzyme is deficient?
questions.explanation: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency (PKU): Phe builds up and tyrosine, hence melanin, falls. The early test was falsely normal because the mother cleared fetal Phe through the placenta (test after 24-48 h of protein feeding). A: Tyrosinase deficiency causes albinism without a musty odor or Phe accumulation. B: Homogentisic acid oxidase deficiency causes alkaptonuria (dark urine, arthritis later). D: This enzyme gives maple syrup urine disease. E: This enzyme gives homocystinuria.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old has displaced lenses, osteoporosis and a deep vein thrombosis. Plasma methionine is high and cysteine is low. Which enzyme is deficient?
questions.explanation: Cystathionine β-synthase converts homocysteine to cystathionine (toward cysteine); its loss raises homocysteine and methionine and lowers cysteine. Pyridoxine (B6) helps responsive patients. A: PAH deficiency is PKU. B: Homogentisic acid oxidase is defective in alkaptonuria. C: This enzyme is defective in maple syrup urine disease. D: Tyrosinase deficiency causes albinism.

questions.stem: A man with recurrent kidney stones excretes cystine, ornithine, arginine and lysine in his urine. Which statement best explains his disease?

options.A: Transporter shared by gut and kidney; ornithine forms stones
options.C: Urea cycle enzyme defect; arginine forms stones
options.D: Transporter shared by gut and kidney; cystine forms stones
options.E: Neutral amino acid transporter defect; tryptophan is lost

questions.explanation: Cystinuria: a defect in the COAL transport system shared by the small intestine and proximal tubule; only cystine is insoluble enough to precipitate. A: Ornithine doesn't precipitate. B: The same transport systems exist in the intestine. C: It's a transport defect, not a urea cycle disorder. E: Neutral amino acid (tryptophan) loss is Hartnup disorder.

questions.stem: During prolonged exercise, skeletal muscle sends amino nitrogen to the liver as alanine. What does the liver do with alanine's carbon skeleton?

options.A: Transaminates it to pyruvate and makes glucose
options.C: Converts it to glutamine for excretion
options.D: Converts it to lactate for the Cori cycle

questions.explanation: Glucose–alanine (Cahill) cycle: muscle transaminates pyruvate to alanine; the liver transaminates alanine back to pyruvate (ALT) and uses it for gluconeogenesis, returning glucose to muscle. B: Only glutamate undergoes rapid oxidative deamination. C: Glutamine is the other ammonia carrier, made by glutamine synthetase in most tissues. D: The Cori cycle carries lactate from muscle to liver, not the reverse. E: Alanine is glucogenic; leucine and lysine are the only exclusively ketogenic amino acids.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old develops a scaly rash on sun-exposed skin, diarrhea and episodes of confusion after a febrile illness. Urine contains increased neutral amino acids. What links his transport defect to the symptoms?

options.A: Cystine precipitates in skin and gut
options.C: Homogentisic acid deposits in connective tissue
options.D: Tryptophan loss limits niacin and NAD⁺ synthesis

questions.explanation: Hartnup disorder: defective neutral amino acid transport in gut and kidney causes loss of tryptophan, a precursor of niacin (nicotinamide of NAD⁺/NADP⁺), so it mimics pellagra. Treatment: high-protein diet, sun protection, niacin. A: Cystine forms kidney stones in cystinuria. B: PKU causes hypopigmentation, not a pellagra-like picture. C: Homogentisic acid pigments cartilage in alkaptonuria. E: Branched-chain keto acids accumulate in maple syrup urine disease.
